Requires Cursor Pro, a public endpoint, and handling of upstream API keys.
Activity is limited (about 30 commits); maintenance and Cursor compatibility are not guaranteed.

aiReview.summary: Community MIT-licensed Go client for DeepSeek’s API (chat, reasoning, tools, FIM, streaming) plus OpenAI-compatible providers. Useful developer tooling, but it is not an official DeepSeek SDK or model card.
evidence: GitHub description and README: Go SDK for DeepSeek V4 API with chat, reasoning, Anthropic endpoint, tool calling, FIM, streaming.
Repo shows tests, CI workflow badge, MIT license, examples/, 338 commits, ~346 stars, 35 forks.
Install path: go get github.com/cohesion-org/deepseek-go.
uncertainty: Whether DeepSeek officially endorses this client.
Live API compatibility and release cadence versus current DeepSeek endpoints.
Production usage quality beyond README examples and CI.
aiReview.tagline: Go client for DeepSeek APIs and compatible providers
aiReview.description: Call DeepSeek chat, reasoning, tools, FIM, and streaming from Go, with OpenRouter, Azure, Ollama, and OpenAI-compatible backends.
pros: Public Go module with chat, Anthropic-compatible client, thinking mode, tool calling, FIM, and streaming documented in the README.
Includes tests, CI badge, examples, CHANGELOG, contributing guide, and MIT license.
Supports extra backends: OpenRouter, Azure, Ollama, and OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
Published on pkg.go.dev with hundreds of commits and a modest star/fork count.
cons: Third-party cohesion-org library, not official DeepSeek documentation or a Hugging Face model card.
Requires a provider API key and currently documents Go 1.26.0.
API-surface claims (e.g. V4 models) depend on upstream DeepSeek changes remaining compatible.

aiReview.summary: Unofficial Node.js local proxy that exposes DeepSeek Web Chat as OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible APIs via a logged-in browser session. Experimental and not official docs or SDKs; ToS and stability risk.
evidence: GitHub ForgetMeAI/FreeDeepseekAPI: ~418 stars, 94 forks, MIT, 49 commits.
README: local API server for chat.deepseek.com via saved browser session; experimental warning.
Features listed: /v1/chat/completions, /v1/messages, /v1/responses, SSE, reasoning_content, tools.
uncertainty: Current ToS compliance of scraping DeepSeek Web Chat.
Maintenance cadence and whether web API still matches the code.
Security of storing deepseek-auth.json / cookies.
aiReview.tagline: Local OpenAI-style proxy over DeepSeek Web Chat
aiReview.description: Run a local Node proxy that maps DeepSeek Web Chat sessions to OpenAI, Anthropic, and Responses APIs with streaming.
pros: Public MIT-licensed Node.js project with README, tests, and zero npm dependencies for the proxy.
Documents OpenAI chat completions, Anthropic Messages, Responses API shims, streaming, and tool calling.
Includes auth via a dedicated Chrome profile, doctor diagnostics, and Open WebUI notes.
cons: Unofficial web-chat reverse proxy using a personal DeepSeek login, not official API or model cards.
README states DeepSeek may change the web API without notice and advises paid official API for production.
Browser-session reuse and multi-account pooling may conflict with DeepSeek terms of use.

aiReview.summary: Community Python CLI that benchmarks TTFT/TBT across several DeepSeek API providers; useful for latency comparison, not official docs or an SDK.
evidence: GitHub description: benchmarking tool for comparing LLM API providers' DeepSeek deployments.
README lists providers, prices, TTFT/TBT metrics, pip install, and bench.py usage.
Repo has 56 commits, MIT license, live demo at deepseek.ai-infra.fun.
uncertainty: Current maintenance cadence and accuracy of listed prices.
Whether live demo stays in sync with the repo.
aiReview.tagline: Compare DeepSeek API provider latency and pricing
aiReview.description: Benchmark TTFT and inter-token time across DeepSeek-compatible API providers with multi-run stats and env-based keys.
pros: Open-source MIT Python tool with README covering install, .env keys, and CLI flags.
Measures TTFT and token-between-time across listed providers including official DeepSeek.
Includes a live demo URL and result/report generation scripts.
cons: Not official DeepSeek documentation, model cards, or a maintained client SDK.
Small GitHub traction (about 31 stars, 0 forks) and depends on third-party provider keys.
Benchmark methodology and prompt set are not independently validated here.

aiReview.summary: Third-party WordPress plugin that wires DeepSeek’s translation API into TranslatePress. Useful for WP sites, but it is not official DeepSeek docs, a model card, or a maintained SDK.
evidence: GitHub description and README: lightweight PHP/WordPress plugin for TranslatePress + DeepSeek API.
README features: batch translation, Automatic Translation engine named DeepSeek Translate, platform.deepseek.com API key.
Repo stats from GitHub page: 19 stars, 7 forks, 23 commits; includes vendor/, composer.json, plugin bootstrap PHP.
uncertainty: Maintenance status, security review of vendor code, and WordPress.org listing not verified.
Actual translation quality and DeepSeek endpoint/model used not independently verified.
aiReview.tagline: WordPress plugin adding DeepSeek translation to TranslatePre
aiReview.description: Integrates DeepSeek’s translation API with TranslatePress for automatic and batch multilingual WordPress content.
pros: Public GitHub repo with README covering install, API key setup, and TranslatePress configuration.
Documents WordPress 6.0+, PHP 7.2+, TranslatePress, and a DeepSeek API key as requirements.
Lists a fixed set of supported language codes and batch-translation behavior.
cons: Community WordPress plugin, not official DeepSeek documentation, model cards, or a language SDK.
Low adoption signals (about 19 stars, 7 forks, 23 commits) and vendors PHP dependencies in-tree.
Language-count claims in the repo description (100+ vs 30+) are inconsistent.

aiReview.summary: Community MIT PHP client for the DeepSeek API (Composer, PHP 8.1+), with fluent builders, PSR-18/Guzzle or Symfony HTTP, streaming, and V4 model support. Useful for PHP apps; it is not an official DeepSeek first-party SDK.
evidence: GitHub deepseek-php/deepseek-php-client: public, MIT, 473 stars, 55 forks, 140 commits, PHP 8.1+.
README: composer require deepseek-php/deepseek-php-client; DeepSeekClient::build()->query()->run(); Models::V4_PRO/V4_FLASH.
Repo includes tests/, docs/, CONTRIBUTING.md, CHANGELOG.md, MIGRATION.md.
uncertainty: Could not independently verify official listing in DeepSeek API docs or Packagist download counts.
Maintenance cadence and production reliability beyond README claims not audited.
PHP not in allowed tags; language is extra.
aiReview.tagline: Community PHP client for DeepSeek chat and models
aiReview.description: Call DeepSeek APIs from PHP 8.1+ with a fluent Composer client, streaming, and Guzzle or Symfony HTTP.
pros: MIT-licensed Composer package with src, tests, phpunit, phpstan, changelog, and migration docs.
Documents fluent usage, streaming, function calling, model listing, and Guzzle or Symfony HTTP clients.
README claims first-class DeepSeek V4 Pro/Flash support and notes deprecation of older chat/R1 aliases.
Packagist-published with ~473 GitHub stars and Laravel/Symfony integration mentioned.
cons: Community-maintained under deepseek-php, not a first-party DeepSeek official SDK.
Legacy CHAT/CODER/R1 models are marked deprecated toward v3.0.0 and API alias retirement in 2026.

aiReview.summary: Unofficial Unity UPM package that wraps the DeepSeek chat API with streaming, samples, and editor key storage. Community-maintained, not official docs or a Hugging Face model card.
evidence: GitHub yagizeraslan/DeepSeek-Unity: unofficial Unity package, MIT, UPM Git URL.
Features listed: SSE streaming, Chat/Reasoner, sample chat scene, EditorPrefs/settings for API keys.
Stars ~36, forks 6; Unity 2020.3+; WebGL streaming unsupported per README.
uncertainty: Last-commit recency and production reliability not independently verified beyond README claims.
API coverage vs current DeepSeek endpoints not audited in source.
aiReview.tagline: Unofficial Unity package for DeepSeek chat and streaming
aiReview.description: Install via UPM to call DeepSeek chat and reasoner models from Unity, with SSE streaming, samples, and editor API-key setup.
pros: MIT-licensed Unity package with Runtime, Editor, Samples, and package.json for UPM Git install.
README documents SSE streaming, Chat and Reasoner models, sample scenes, and Unity 2020.3+ requirements.
Repo has a changelog, 138 commits, and states it is unofficial and unaffiliated with DeepSeek.
cons: Community Unity client, not official DeepSeek docs, model cards, or first-party SDKs.
Low adoption (about 36 stars, 6 forks) and several platforms listed as untested.
WebGL streaming is limited; API usage still depends on a paid DeepSeek platform key.

aiReview.summary: Community scripts to export, INT8-quantize, and run DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B on Huawei Ascend Atlas 200I DK A2 (OM). Niche hardware demo, not official docs or a maintained SDK.
evidence: GitHub description and README: R1 1.5B, INT8, OM on Atlas 200I DK A2.
Files include export.py, quant.py, eval.py, generate.py, and *.cc CANN plugins.
Repo stats observed: public, ~16 stars, 1 fork, 10 commits.
uncertainty: License file not confirmed from the listing.
Maintenance status and whether ATC/OM conversion still works on current CANN.
aiReview.tagline: INT8 OM inference of R1 1.5B on Ascend Atlas
aiReview.description: Export DeepSeek R1 1.5B to ONNX, quantize to INT8, and deploy OM inference on Ascend Atlas 200I DK A2.
pros: README documents ONNX export, INT8 quantization, eval, and custom CANN plugins for missing operators.
Targets DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B on Atlas 200I DK A2 / 310B-class devices.
Public GitHub repo with Python and C++ plugin sources.
cons: Not official DeepSeek documentation, a model card, or a general-purpose SDK.
Low activity (~16 stars, ~10 commits) and hardware-specific CANN/ATC setup.
Users must download weights separately; OM conversion depends on custom operators.

Content is a third-party interpretation of public materials, not first-party API or model facts.
